faq.q: What are the three ways to make a signature?
faq.a: Draw (mouse or finger, with smooth pressure/velocity-aware strokes, selectable ink colour — black, dark blue or blue — and pen width 1–8), Type (your name in one of five cursive fonts: Dancing Script, Great Vibes, Sacramento, Caveat or Satisfy, with size and colour controls), or Upload a photo of your signature, where a light background is removed automatically using an adjustable threshold.

faq.q: How do I meet a government form's size requirements?
faq.a: Use the output options: auto-crop to the signature, or fixed presets like 140×60px (government forms), 300×80px or 500×200px, plus a padding choice. Download as JPG (white background) for portals that require it — the tool notes forms often need under 30 KB and JPG format. A tip explains SSC-style signatures are roughly 6cm×2cm.

faq.q: Should I pick PNG or JPG?
faq.a: PNG gives a transparent background so the signature drops onto any document; JPG fills the background white. Important: JPG has no transparency, so a transparent signature becomes black if saved as JPG — the tool's notes highlight this common mistake. You can also copy the signature to the clipboard as a transparent PNG.

faq.q: Is this a legally binding digital signature?
faq.a: No. This produces an image of a signature, which is fine as a specimen to upload to a form, but it is not a cryptographic digital signature like a DSC token or Aadhaar eSign that binds a document to an identity. The notes explain the difference. Everything runs in your browser — the image is never uploaded — and only style preferences (not the signature itself) are saved locally.
